John Stockton.text: The Jazz made the playoffs in every one of his 19 seasons.
John Stockton.evidence: Regarded as one of the greatest point guards of all time, he spent his entire NBA career (1984–2003) with the Utah Jazz. The team made the playoffs in each of his 19 seasons.

Chris Paul.text: A 2011 trade sending him to the Lakers was voided by the NBA, which owned his team at the time.
Chris Paul.evidence: During the 2011 offseason, the Hornets organized a deal to send Paul to the Los Angeles Lakers, but the transaction was controversially voided by the NBA (which temporarily owned the team at the time).

Jason Kidd.text: Won his only NBA championship at age 38, with Dallas in 2011.
Jason Kidd.evidence: At age 38, Kidd won his only NBA championship when Dallas defeated the Miami Heat in the 2011 NBA Finals.

LeBron James.text: The first player to win Finals MVP with three different teams.
LeBron James.evidence: He signed with the Los Angeles Lakers in 2018, winning another title in 2020 and becoming the first player to win Finals MVP with three different teams.

Russell Westbrook.text: The NBA's all-time leader in career triple-doubles.
Russell Westbrook.evidence: Westbrook is one of three players in NBA history to average a triple-double for a season, a feat he achieved four times and is the all-time NBA leader in career triple-doubles.

Mark Jackson.text: Before free throws he would extend a hand and "cup" his thumb and index finger around the rim.
Mark Jackson.evidence: While at St. John's, Jackson developed an unusual free-throw line ritual of extending his hand and "cupping" his thumb and index finger around the rim. This helped him stay focused on the rim while shooting foul shots.

Magic Johnson.text: Retired in 1991 after announcing he had HIV, then came back for the 1992 All-Star Game and won its MVP.
Magic Johnson.evidence: Johnson retired abruptly in 1991 after announcing that he had contracted HIV, but returned to play in the 1992 All-Star Game, winning the All-Star MVP Award.
